# Approved jelly oracle

`approved-jelly.json` was captured from the original v9 brainstorming HTML.
Its unchanged draw function and initial state are preserved in `approved-v9.js`,
outside ignored session directories. It is not generated by the extracted
artwork/compositor. A fresh clone can verify or regenerate all 42 reference frames.

`bun tests/fixtures/capture-approved.ts --write` executes v9's existing `draw`
in a local VM with an opaque integer canvas shim. `since = 0` and all calls to
`draw(canvas, ms)` run in one synchronous evaluation. Reduced motion is explicitly
off. Both hat choices cover every mood, plus glances, blinks, bob, hop, recoil,
and transient expiry. Without `--write`, the command verifies the fixture against
v9 without changing it. Keep the checked-in fixture stable during refactoring.

On 2026-09-10, a follow-up check loaded this preserved v9 HTML as an actual
Chromium page over a temporary localhost HTTP server. Playwright explicitly set
`reducedMotion: 'no-preference'`; one synchronous page evaluation set `since = 0`,
selected each fixture's mood/hat, called the page's original `draw(canvas, ms)`,
and read `getImageData(0, 0, 24, 24)`. All 42 cases / 24,192 pixels / 96,768 RGBA
channels matched exactly (including transparent RGBA `[0, 0, 0, 0]`). Neither the
preview nor fixture was overwritten. This establishes browser equivalence of
the earlier VM capture; it is not a claim of pre-refactor browser capture.
Full method/results are in
`.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-10-blue-jelly/task-1-report.md`, review follow-up section.
